stage: Product review performed after color_controls explicit freeze, before parent-owned SDK formatting and validation.

summary.result: No additional reproducible source defect found in the frozen queue/manual soft-stop implementations or their owner/generation/job/actor cleanup. Parent owns runtime validation.

originalTrigger: A manual camera.download is still held when its original tool is closed; dispose now requests ordinary soft-stop and the global manual lease remains until drain.
The user opens another connection page and explicitly chooses Disconnect.
The former disconnect implementation stopped queue/live only and then queued Native camera.disconnect behind the held camera transaction. It did not invoke the old manual lease hard-stop callback.
findings.originalImpact: An explicit disconnect could wait behind old camera I/O rather than cancelling its exact job. This was distinct from an ordinary soft-stop.

currentEvidence.guards: Mounted/epoch checked immediately after manual stop, after queue hard-stop, and after Live hard-stop.
currentEvidence.nativeDisconnect: Retains captured expectedSession in camera.disconnect payload.

checks.conclusion: resume assigns the raw run Future before changed(). Only its returned _settledRun wrapper waits for that run epoch StopC; stop awaits raw running, so there is no run-waits-stop/stop-waits-wrapper cycle.

Soft-stop increments generation and retains busy until raw drain, scoped pause and actor release finish. Every awaited boundary rechecks generation plus StopC identity. Final completion clears only its own StopC. A newly admitted resume cannot be overwritten by the old stop after changed().

Retired old run finally always cancels its own event subscription; shared busy/job/actor changes remain epoch guarded. connectionLost clears busy and its StopC pointer locally, allowing a replacement run while old closures retain their own completion handles.

Hard-upgrade targets the precise current job and deduplicates cancellation per stop. A late cancellation failure can update error only with alive/owner/generation/StopC identity still matching. Account change uses explicit hard stop then local retirement and clears old display state.

start always completes its private run completion in finally before joining its matching StopC at the tail; stop waits that private completion rather than the public start Future. This breaks circular waiting even if stop starts during a held RPC.

Old-generation run finally does not clear busy/job or release the global lease. The owning StopC releases that lease once after drain. Normal completion releases before any reentrant new admission, and subsequent old cleanup uses completion identity/epoch checks.

The global onStop callback accepts hard upgrade during an existing soft stop even though canStop is false after _stopped. A normal local importing/publication phase with no StopC retains its original completion boundary. Camera job is cleared only by matching RPC finally.

Owner changes invalidate visible data and request exact hard cancellation. Saved Photo is installed only after _check(epoch) succeeds; stale owner/run results cannot repopulate importedPhoto. Hard ACK error handling is owner/epoch/StopC guarded.

connectCamera/openConnection return bool. Closing/cancelling the route returns false; Live host requests loadPhotos:false and waitForStatus:false, so it does not wait on parent photo/status loading before acting on a confirmed connection result.

stopCameraManualTransfer compares expectedSession before invoking the captured stop callback, and waits for that unique lease to change. Root disconnect passes the captured session, preserving the old/new lease boundary.

routing.sourceConclusion: This review writes only its report. Queue/manual changes use existing exact-id cancellation only for explicit hard-stop and preserve default ordinary drain; root Native disconnect retains strict session payload. No Android Wi-Fi socket routing or public-network selection was changed by this review.
